# Can documentation fill a compiled-code hole? Synthesis for the 1 Beyond IV-CAM V2 experiment

## 1. The headline: calibration passed on protocol constants, failed on device physics — and produced one outright contradiction

The control group is 26 declared Transformations in `driver_definition.Transformations` of `/Users/robp/GitHub/rob-paprocki/extron-driver-convert/samples/Crestron 1 Beyond IV-CAM-i12_i20/Crestron/Camera_Crestron-1-Beyond_IV-CAM-I20_IP.pkg` (verified count: 26; P20 has 27). Raw score from the calibration pass, independently re-verified: **12 fully predicted, 5 partial, 9 not predicted** — 46% strict, 56% weighted.

That raw number understates and overstates in opposite directions, so re-partition it. Five of the 26 never touch the wire at all (`RoundToInt`, `RoundToTenths`, `MapPanDirectionToValue`, `MapTiltDirectionToValue`, `InvertBoolean`) — a VISCA command reference cannot be expected to document a driver's internal signed-direction representation, and counting them as doc failures is unfair. Of the **21 wire-facing** transformations: **11 fully predicted (52%), 4 partial, 1 contradicted, 5 not predicted.**

The pattern inside those numbers is sharp and it is the actual result:

**Predicted reliably** — anything that is a repeated protocol constant appearing across many rows of the command tables. `MapBooleanToViscaOnOff` 0x02/0x03 (four independent families: CAM_Power, CAM_ExpComp, CAM_Backlight, IR_Receive, `reference/crestron-visca/COMMANDS.md` lines 139-140, 194-195, 200-201, 209-210). `MapExposureMode` 00/03/0A/0B matching CAM_AE byte for byte, including the driver's own comment. `MapFocusDirection` 02/03/00. `MapZoomSpeedZoomDirection` 0x20-0x27 / 0x30-0x37 against `07 2p FF` / `07 3p FF`. `MapPanDirection` / `MapTiltDirection` decomposed exactly from all nine Pan-tiltDrive rows. `PanTiltAngleToPosition` Operand 14.4, literally in the doc (`reference/crestron-visca/VISCA-Commands.md` lines 582/592, misfiled on the wrong rows). `MapTrackingFramingProfileToPreset` → 0x69-0x6C via `Reserved-Presets.md` 105-108 plus the doc's own stated decimal-to-hex step.

**Not predicted at all** — anything device-specific: `MapAutoFocusBehavior` (00/01/04; no page documents an AF-area submode concept, grep-confirmed across all 16 files), `MapModelCodeToModel` (0505/0506/0507/0508; CAM_VersionInq's reply structure is documented, the code values are not), and — this is the one that matters most — `ZoomPositionToFieldOfView` / `FieldOfViewToZoomPosition`, whose Polynomial endpoints 4.159363682153226° / 67.07093698846305° appear nowhere; the spec pages give one static 56.45° figure.

**Contradicted** — `MapIndicatorLightToLedBar`. The driver sends 00 0D 0D 00 for red/3/Half; `VISCA-Lightbar-Commands.md` requires 01 0D 0D 01, and 03 0F 0F 03 where the driver sends 00 0F 0F 00. Green agrees only because green's colour code is coincidentally 0x00. This is the most important single result in the calibration set, and it is a *failure mode the Automate VX work never surfaced*: the documentation was not silent, it was specific and wrong at byte level. A converter that used a doc-derived library as a silent fallback would have emitted different bytes than the shipped driver and called it a success.

**Verdict: conditional trust, scoped by category.** The docs are a trustworthy source for repeated wire constants, an untrustworthy source for analogue curves and vendor-assigned codes, and — where most specific — occasionally wrong. That scoping is what makes the rest of this report worth reading, and it is also why the answer to the headline question is a qualified no: on the six IL-only holes, **the documentation's only original contribution was the zoom-ratio table**, and that contribution lands squarely in the untrustworthy category.

## 2. Which of the six are recoverable, and what would settle the rest

Safe to build on — **two of six**, and note carefully where the evidence came from:

**`ViscaAssemble2LowerNibbles`** = `(b[0] & 0x0F) << 4 | (b[1] & 0x0F)`. Pinned by `Responses[26]` (`ViscaTrackingFramingProfileInquiryResponse`), whose regex captures `\x06[\x09-\x0c]`, feeding the *declared* map `MapTrackingFramingProfileToPreset` = {i, j, k, l} = 0x69-0x6C. Four data points; the two plausible alternative nibble orders both fail. This is CONFIRMED. Note that the algorithm falls out of the JSON alone — the doc's `Reserved-Presets.md` only labels the presets. The dossier's "second independent confirmation" via the COMMANDS.md 28F6 zoom check was correctly downgraded on review: that check is circular (the nibbles were produced by splitting the target value's own hex digits) and COMMANDS.md itself labels it as derived, not vendor-stated.

**`ParseDecimal`** — a no-op numeric coercion. `Rules[27]`, Transformations[2], input and output are both `{ZoomPositionPollingOnly}`, immediately preceding a Polynomial that needs a numeric argument; the value originates as a `FromBytesToUInt` output in `Responses[10]` and is already integral. Recovered from the JSON, not the doc. Trivially portable.

Not recoverable — **four of six**:

**`FormatRomVersion`.** Correct the dossier here: the doc-vs-driver agent claimed this transformation lives in the undocumented `c2 09` register block, and that is refuted by its own citation. `GetDeviceInformation` resolves to `ViscaInquiry` with Parameters `00 02`, i.e. `8x 09 00 02 FF` — Crestron's documented CAM_VersionInq (`COMMANDS.md` line 269), and the doc even gives the byte position of the 2-byte ROM field, matching the `RomVersion` regex capture in `Responses[19]` exactly. What is undocumented is only the *display convention* for those two bytes; the property `deviceInformation:firmwareVersion` has typeDef `{"type": "string"}` with no format constraint. The Aver cross-vendor snippet cited as circumstantial support has no retrievable URL and left no artifact under `reference/crestron-visca/` — under the project's own citation rule it should be struck. **Settled by:** one live CAM_VersionInq capture against the unit's displayed firmware label. Risk class: cosmetic — a wrong guess mis-renders a string, it cannot emit bad bytes.

**`ApplyZoomPositionStep`.** Contract pinned exactly (`Rules[20-23]`, `Controllers` FieldOfView ToDeviceTransformations[2]; args are the computed float, `{Model}`, and a literal Set/Increment/Decrement). Algorithm unpinned. Round-and-clamp to [0, 16384] is functionally correct at every gated call site because `Conditions[17]` and `Conditions[19]` already bound the range; a wrong step rule produces a stuck-zoom UX bug, not an out-of-range packet. **Settled by:** a bench sweep, or a second V2 PTZ driver that expresses the same step rule declaratively.

**`ZoomLevelToPosition` / `ZoomPositionToLevel`.** Split. For the optical range the doc's 20-point Zoom Ratio table (`COMMANDS.md` §6, 1x=0x0000 to 20x=0x4000) is real evidence and a piecewise-linear fit reproduces all 20 breakpoints exactly. **But piecewise-linear is one of several curve families equally consistent with 20 points**, and this SDK's own `Polynomial` transformation type is evidence the house style may be a smooth fit. Between breakpoints, error is unbounded and unmeasured — and these values *are* emitted as CAM_Zoom Direct nibbles. This is exactly the project's worst failure mode: plausible, checkable at 20 points, wrong in between. Do not ship it. For the digital range (16384-31424, per `Controllers` ZoomPosition Min/Max, with ZoomLevel Max = 320.0 confirmed by `Rules[31]` under Condition ModelIsP20OrI20) there is **zero** documentation; grep for "digital zoom" across the harvest returns nothing, and the spec pages say 20x optical. Also correct the dossier's mitigation: the claim that only `ZoomPositionToLevel`'s digital range is live is **overstated**. `Rules[22]` (ProcessZoomPositionIncrement, CommandTypes ["Increment"]) calls `ZoomLevelToPosition` gated only on the *pre*-increment position, and `Rules[26]` (FeedbackForZoomLevel, unconditional) keeps ZoomLevel synced across the full 0-31424 range, so both directions have live paths above 20x. **Settled by:** a bench sweep of CAM_ZoomPosInq against displayed zoom level across the whole range — one capture settles both transformations *and* ApplyZoomPositionStep's quantisation.

## 3. What this does to "Crestron in" for SDK V2

Concrete, measured on the I20 (P20 differs by one name):

Of 39 distinct Transformation names referenced anywhere in Rules/Commands/Responses/Controllers, **26 are declared in the JSON** (66.7%), and every declared transformation is actually used (declared-but-unused = 0). The 13 undeclared split three ways: five generic SDK arithmetic primitives (`Identity`, `Sum`, `Subtract`, `Product`, `Divide`), two framework VISCA helpers (`ViscaExtractNibbles`, `ViscaAssemble4LowerNibbles`), and six driver-local IL names. Weighted by invocation site (140 total): declared 75 sites (53.6%), SDK arithmetic 32 (22.9%), framework VISCA 19 (13.6%), **driver-local IL 14 sites (10.0%)**.

So the tractable fraction with a per-vendor primitives library is 33/39 names (84.6%) or 126/140 sites (90.0%). This experiment moves **2 of the 6 IL-only names** to safe, taking it to 35/39 names (89.7%) and 128/140 sites (91.4%). The residual is 4 names / 12 sites — about **8.6% of invocation sites**, concentrated entirely in the zoom subsystem plus one cosmetic string.

That is a real gain, but the honest framing is that the gain came almost entirely from **mining the driver's own declarative sections**, not from the documentation. The doc's one original contribution to the six holes (the zoom-ratio table) is precisely the contribution that is not safe to ship.

**What a converter should do when it meets an undeclared transformation — three tiers, and never a doc fallback:**

Tier 1, a **named vendor library** for the framework/SDK primitives, implemented once and verified per driver wherever a declared map provides a cross-check (as `MapTrackingFramingProfileToPreset` did for nibble assembly). Note a live ambiguity even here: `ViscaExtractNibbles`'s templates (`04 48 {Y4}{Y3}{Y2}{Y1}`) match the doc's `04 48 0p 0q 0r 0s` structurally, but the JSON alone does not establish which of Y4/Y1 is most-significant. Treat it as Tier 2 until a cross-check pins it.

Tier 2, a **special-cased known set** for driver-local IL names, each carrying a provenance tag (JSON-derived / doc-derived / inferred) and a confidence level, each gated on a cross-check that must pass at conversion time.

Tier 3, **fail loudly** with the exact name list. Finding 07's "enumerate referenced minus declared" rule is right and should be upgraded: enumeration alone is not enough, the diff must be *classified* into these tiers, and Tier 3 must be a hard stop, never a best-effort emission.

**Explicitly rejected: a doc-derived library consulted as a silent fallback.** The lightbar case is the proof. Documentation may be used to *explain* and to *cross-check* a reconstruction; it may not be used to *generate* bytes.

One limit on all of this: n = 2, and both drivers are the same 1 Beyond engine (same SDK 26.0.26.0, same 11-section schema). Finding 08's claim that the residue is "a small, reusable, per-vendor set" is supported for this camera family and is *not* established for the SDK V2 catalogue at large.

## 4. Did the doc-versus-driver delta reproduce?

Yes, bidirectionally, and with a new and worse variant.

**Driver as superset.** Both drivers use vendor-extension `c2` sub-opcodes `02` (AF behaviour), `03` (AF sensitivity), `04` (auto software update), `06` (group tracking), `07` (tracking framing profile, I20 only), and `01 0a` (Identify) — none documented anywhere, and *disjoint* from the sub-opcodes Crestron does document for Intelligent Switching (08, 09, 0A, 0B, 0d). Crestron carved the same extension byte into two ranges and documented only the one this driver never uses. Add `GetAutoPrivacyMode` / `SetAutoPrivacyMode` (`0e 24 26 00 {OnOff}`), also undocumented — which walks back the dossier's claim that privacy is "entirely mechanical"; the mechanical tilt-to-max PrivacyCommand is real, but it is not the only privacy path.

**Driver as subset.** Neither driver implements White Balance, RGain/BGain, manual Shutter/Iris/Gain/Bright, Backlight, IR_Receive, Pan-tiltLimitSet, combined CAM_ZoomFocus, or any of the eight documented Intelligent Switching commands (82 commands enumerated on I20, 77 on P20).

**Direct contradictions.** The lightbar off-segment bytes; and the range conflict — `Controllers` ZoomPosition Max = 31424 and ZoomLevel Max = 320.0 against spec pages that say 20x optical and a doc table that ends at 16384 — with the driver's own FieldOfView controller still using 0-16384, so the JSON is not even internally consistent.

**Where it differs from findings 08.** On the Automate VX the doc's failure was *silence* (Wake undocumented while Sleep is), and silence is survivable because a converter notices. Here the docs got the majority of wire-facing declared bytes right — the best doc performance of the three data points — and then were confidently, specifically wrong on the one table where they gave a fully worked example. The project's standing rule survives intact and strengthened: **where driver and doc disagree, the shipped driver is the record of what the device does.**

## 5. Amendments to findings 07 and 08, and the next step

**Finding 07** (`/Users/robp/GitHub/rob-paprocki/extron-driver-convert/findings/07-1beyond-and-simpl.md`): the "six Transformations have no declarative definition" line is correct but incomplete — record the full classification (39 referenced, 26 declared, 13 undeclared = 5 SDK arithmetic + 2 framework VISCA + 6 driver-local IL; 140 invocation sites, 14 of them driver-local IL). Upgrade the design rule from "fail loudly with the list of IL-only names" to the three-tier scheme in section 3.

**Finding 08** (`/Users/robp/GitHub/rob-paprocki/extron-driver-convert/findings/08-spec-vs-implementation.md`): add a third data point to "The IL-only residue is bounded and reusable" — 2 of 6 now recoverable *without decompilation*, recovered from the JSON's declarative sections rather than from documentation, with the residual isolated to the zoom subsystem plus one cosmetic string. Add the new sub-finding that documentation can be *checkably wrong at byte level*, not merely silent (lightbar), and record the resulting prohibition on doc-derived fallback generation. Refine the section's thesis: documentation is reliable for repeated protocol constants, unreliable for device-specific curves and vendor-assigned codes, and least reliable exactly where it is most specific. Also fold in the correction that `FormatRomVersion` reads a *documented* command; only the string format is undocumented.

**Single highest-value next step: broaden the SDK V2 corpus.** The repo holds exactly two V2 packages and they are the same engine, yet the whole "Crestron in" tractability estimate rests on them. Harvesting 15-30 SDK V2 driver packages across vendors from Crestron's driver database (via Bright Data, per the access rule) and re-running the referenced-minus-declared classification does three things at once: it tests whether the residue set is per-vendor or per-SDK-version, it builds the Tier 1 primitives inventory empirically, and — the real prize — it may find a PTZ driver that expresses its zoom curve as a **declared `Polynomial`**, which would settle `ZoomLevelToPosition` / `ZoomPositionToLevel` on the optical range with no hardware and no decompilation. It costs no hardware and no licence risk.

The bench capture stays on the list as the only route to the residual, and it is one session: CAM_VersionInq reply bytes against the unit's displayed firmware string, a CAM_ZoomPosInq sweep across 0-31424 against displayed zoom level, and the lightbar half-width red/yellow behaviour. That settles four of the six holes and the one calibration contradiction — but it is gated on hardware the project does not currently have, and the corpus scan may remove part of its scope first.

**Safe to build on:** the calibration's category verdict, `ViscaAssemble2LowerNibbles`, `ParseDecimal`, the referenced-vs-declared classification and its counts, and the three-tier converter policy. **Not safe to build on:** any zoom-curve reconstruction (optical or digital), any `ApplyZoomPositionStep` step rule, any `FormatRomVersion` string format, and `ViscaExtractNibbles`'s nibble order.
